To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the N‐ras 49–73 peptide with codon 61 mutation is a promiscuous H‐2 class II binding peptide that induces strong DTH reactions and in vitro T‐cell responses in melanoma patients; (2) GM‐CSF can be used as adjuvant in intradermal immunization of melanoma patients; and (3) intradermal immunizations are safe and simple to perform.

we could induce a specific immune response against a mutated ras protein in 2 melanoma patients using a combination of intradermal injection with GM‐CSF and a promiscuous H‐LA class II binding ras peptide as antigen.

we have shown that intradermal injection with GM‐CSF is a feasible method to induce immune responses against mutant N‐ras in melanoma patients, that the immune response is not restricted by the HLA‐types of the patients, and that this method is safe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of melanoma specific antigens and the development of immunotherapeutic strategies.
the development of a vaccine against melanoma based on mutant ras‐peptides and GM‐CS‐F as adjuvants.
the development of a melanoma‐specific peptide vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intradermal injection with ras peptides and GM‐CF as adjuvant may be useful in the immunotherapy of melanoma.
the induction of an immune response towards a melanoma‐specific antigen using a simple and efficient vaccination strategy is feasible and may have clinical relevance.
intradermal injection with GM‐CSF of N‐ras peptides is a feasible and promising approach for immunization against melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of ras‐derived peptides as a vaccine for melanoma patients seems to be a promising approach.
we have been able to induce an immune reaction towards a mutant ras‐protein in a group of melanoma patients using GM‐CSFs as an adjuvant.
we were successful in inducing immune responses against mutant N‐ras in melanoma patients.

the use of mutant ras peptides in combination with GM‐CSF may be a promising approach to induce immune responses in melanoma patients.
